name: Moksy Limited: how the company works
description: What Moksy stands for, how it decides, protects data, handles money, hires, works and manages risk.

groups.people: kind of person in Moksy's vocabulary

cards.subject: Moksy's mission
says: states that most software fails in the specification, not the implementation
frames the work as turning an idea into a build-ready plan
cards.use: explain in one breath why Moksy exists
not: says Moksy builds the finished software for its customers

cards.subject: The 1:99 goal
says: aims for 99 percent of the work to be done by machine and 1 percent by a human
is the founder's stated target for automation
cards.use: need the founder's stated target for how much work the machine does
not: is a target of one customer in ninety-nine converting to a paid plan

cards.subject: The decidedBy stamp
says: records on every decision whether a machine or a human made it
supplies the measurement behind the 1:99 goal
cards.use: need to show how much of the work the machine really did
not: records which customer approved a Blueprint

cards.subject: Moksy's neutrality
says: rests on being the only voice in the search results not selling the build
is described in the sources as the whole advantage
cards.use: are asked why Moksy never takes a side among builders
not: comes from Moksy owning an agency that can build the plan

cards.subject: The never-recommend-a-builder rule
says: bars Moksy from recommending any builder
extends to a sister company
cards.use: are tempted to point a customer to a company Moksy is related to
not: allows a recommendation when the builder is affiliated with Moksy

cards.subject: The Free plan promise
says: makes the Free plan a real plan rather than a demo
gives the same engine reporting on fewer areas so a customer can judge the thinking
cards.use: hear the Free plan described as a demo
not: reports on every area of the Blueprint

cards.subject: The no-rights rule
says: says Moksy claims no rights over a customer's plan or the idea behind it
holds on every plan
cards.use: are asked who owns a customer's idea
not: gives Moksy ownership of plans made on the Free plan

cards.subject: The guide ending
says: closes every guide on the point that a range is not your number
sends readers to the free Blueprint to get their own figure
cards.use: write the last section of a cost guide
not: ends with a quoted price for the reader's project

cards.subject: A positioning statement
says: says who a product is for, what it is and how it differs from the alternatives
is an internal tool rather than a public slogan
cards.use: need to explain how a product differs in its market
not: is the short public line shown beside a logo

cards.subject: A tagline
says: is the short public line that sums up what a company offers
can be retired and replaced when the wording changes
cards.use: need one memorable line for a page header
not: is the registered legal name of the company

cards.subject: A mission statement
says: states why an organisation exists today
answers what the organisation does and for whom
cards.use: need to say why the organisation exists
not: describes the future the organisation hopes to reach

cards.subject: A vision statement
says: describes the future the organisation is working towards
looks further ahead than a mission statement
cards.use: need to describe where the organisation wants to be in the long run
not: lists the tasks a team will do this quarter

cards.subject: The content-and-search growth motion
says: treats growth as a content and search problem
leads readers from guides to a free Blueprint
cards.use: are asked how Moksy expects to win customers
not: relies mainly on outbound sales calls

cards.subject: The outbound-sales non-goal
says: is ruled out because outbound cannot reach the subscriber count the published prices require
keeps the team from building a sales-call machine
cards.use: are asked to start cold-calling prospects for Moksy
not: is the main way Moksy plans to find Pro subscribers

cards.subject: Paid social at Moksy
says: is not part of the documented growth motion
must earn its place against the same numbers if it is tested
cards.use: are asked to launch a Facebook or Instagram test
not: is the main channel for acquiring Pro subscribers

cards.subject: The evidence rule for ads
says: allows an ad to describe only what exists and can be evidenced
requires every figure in an ad to come from a source
cards.use: draft an ad that mentions a feature still being planned
not: lets an ad promise a feature as long as it is on the roadmap

cards.subject: The four-eight-twelve-week review
says: reviews guide results at 4, 8 and 12 weeks
expects nothing for the first four to eight weeks because earlier numbers measure the crawler's schedule
cards.use: are asked why a new guide shows no results after two weeks
not: judges a guide by its first week of impressions

cards.subject: The guide results chain
says: follows impressions, then clicks, then Blueprints, then Pro
gives each stage of the funnel its own number
cards.use: need to trace where readers drop out between a guide and a Pro upgrade
not: follows the chain from Pro upgrade back to paid social

cards.subject: The Free Blueprint started KPI
says: counts customers who begin a free Blueprint
sits between clicks and Pro upgrades in the guide results chain
cards.use: need the number showing how many visitors start a Blueprint
not: counts customers who move up to the Pro plan

cards.subject: The Pro upgrade KPI
says: counts customers who move up to the Pro plan
sits at the end of the guide results chain
cards.use: need the number showing how many customers pay for Pro
not: counts customers who begin a free Blueprint

cards.subject: The machine-share KPI
says: tracks the share of decisions made by machine against the 99 percent target
is read from the decidedBy stamp
cards.use: need to show progress towards the 1:99 goal
not: tracks the share of customers who choose Expert Review

cards.subject: A non-goal
says: states something an organisation deliberately will not do
keeps a team from drifting into side projects
cards.use: need to record what the team has decided not to pursue
not: is a goal that has been missed

cards.subject: A KPI
says: is a measure chosen to show progress against a goal
needs a target and an owner to be actionable
cards.use: need a number that shows whether a goal is being met
not: is a list of tasks for the coming sprint

cards.subject: A leading indicator
says: moves before the result it predicts
gives early warning while there is still time to act
cards.use: need an early signal of whether a goal is on track
not: reports a result only after it has happened

cards.subject: A lagging indicator
says: reports a result after it has happened
confirms an outcome rather than predicting it
cards.use: need to confirm whether a goal was reached
not: moves before the result it predicts

cards.subject: Decision rights
says: state who is allowed to make which decision
prevent a decision being made twice or by nobody
cards.use: are unsure who may approve a change
not: describe how a decision is announced afterwards

cards.subject: A RACI chart
says: assigns each task a responsible, accountable, consulted and informed party
names exactly one accountable owner per task
cards.use: need to show who does the work, who answers for it and who is only told
not: lists the order in which problems move upward

cards.subject: An escalation path
says: defines who to go to when a problem cannot be solved at the current level
sets the order in which problems move upward
cards.use: cannot resolve an issue within your own authority
not: assigns every task an accountable owner

cards.subject: Separation of duties
says: stops one person completing every step of a sensitive process
reduces the chance of undetected error or fraud
cards.use: find one person who can both raise and approve a payment
not: requires two people to sit in the same meeting

cards.subject: The four-eyes principle
says: requires a second person to approve a sensitive action before it takes effect
makes one person's mistake visible before it lands
cards.use: need a second pair of eyes before a risky change goes live
not: stops one person owning every step of a process

cards.subject: The senior-reviewer ruling
says: settles whether a disputed review counts as accepted
is made by a senior reviewer rather than by the original reviewer
cards.use: must settle a disagreement between a customer and a reviewer about a review
not: is made by the customer who raised the dispute

cards.subject: The super-admin pin
says: fixes a user at a chosen level
freezes the automatic computation of that user's level
cards.use: need to hold a reviewer at a level regardless of their score
not: lets a reviewer approve their own accreditation

cards.subject: A pending founder decision
says: records an open product choice awaiting the founder
covers questions such as whether to open any path to withdrawable MOX
cards.use: find an open product question with no decision yet
not: is a choice the founder has already made and published

cards.subject: An audit trail
says: records who did what and when
lets a past decision be reconstructed
cards.use: need to work out who changed a record last month
not: prevents a decision from being made

cards.subject: Delegation of authority
says: passes a defined decision right to another person within set limits
leaves accountability with the person who delegated
cards.use: are away and someone must approve spending in your place
not: transfers accountability completely to the delegate

cards.subject: The support address
says: handles account, plan, billing, review and broken-feature problems
is where customers send their account email and a link to the plan or review
cards.use: help a customer who cannot sign in or sees an unexpected charge
not: receives privacy and data requests

cards.subject: The privacy address
says: receives privacy and data requests
cards.use: handle a customer who asks for a copy of their personal data
not: handles billing disputes

cards.subject: The legal address
says: answers questions about the terms
cards.use: answer a customer who asks what a clause in the terms means
not: receives account and sign-in problems

cards.subject: Sales
says: takes buying questions such as pricing and procurement
cards.use: help a buyer who asks about procurement for a large team
not: handles reviewer payment problems

cards.subject: The help centre
says: holds most answers before a ticket is needed
is the first place support points customers
cards.use: answer a customer who asks a common how-to question
not: is where disputed reviews are decided

cards.subject: Quoting published pages
says: has support quote the published page and say so when pages disagree
avoids stating a figure as settled when sources conflict
cards.use: find that two published pages give different figures for the same thing
not: has support pick whichever figure sounds more reasonable

cards.subject: The account email and plan link
says: are what a customer includes so support can find the case
make a plan or review report traceable
cards.use: help a customer who reports a problem with one particular Blueprint
not: are optional details support never needs

cards.subject: UK GDPR
says: is the UK law governing how personal data is handled
is the regulation cited in Moksy's privacy documents
cards.use: need the main data protection law for Moksy's customers
not: is a voluntary industry code of conduct

cards.subject: A data controller
says: decides why and how personal data is processed
is the role the privacy policy gives Moksy AI Ltd
cards.use: need to know who is responsible for deciding how data is used
not: handles personal data only on someone else's instructions

cards.subject: A data processor
says: handles personal data only on a controller's instructions
cards.use: use a supplier that stores customer data on a company's behalf
not: decides the purposes of processing for itself

cards.subject: A sub-processor
says: is a supplier engaged to process personal data on the company's behalf
needs 30 days' notice at Moksy before one is added
cards.use: plan to add a new supplier that will touch customer data
not: can be added without telling customers

cards.subject: The named sub-processors
says: include OpenAI, Stripe, MongoDB Atlas and Redis
cards.use: are asked which suppliers handle customer data
not: are limited to Moksy's own employees

cards.subject: Article 33
says: sets a 72-hour window for breach notification once the organisation becomes aware
is the article Moksy cites for notifying controllers of a personal-data breach
cards.use: discover a personal-data breach and must plan who to tell and when
not: gives the organisation 30 days to investigate before telling anyone

cards.subject: The ICO
says: is the UK regulator customers may complain to about data handling
cards.use: advise a customer who is unhappy with how their data was handled and wants to escalate
not: is the payment processor for Moksy plans

cards.subject: A data subject request
says: is a person's request for access, correction, deletion, objection, restriction or portability
goes to the privacy address at Moksy
cards.use: handle a customer who asks for their personal data to be deleted
not: is a request to change a plan, which goes to Sales

cards.subject: Data minimisation
says: limits the personal data collected to what is needed
reduces what could be exposed in a breach
cards.use: are asked to add another field to a sign-up form
not: means collecting all the data that might be useful later

cards.subject: A strictly necessary cookie
says: may be set without consent
is needed for the service to work as the user asked
cards.use: are deciding which cookies need a consent banner
not: always needs explicit consent

cards.subject: An analytics cookie
says: needs explicit consent before it is set
measures how visitors use the site
cards.use: are adding visitor tracking to a page
not: may be set without consent because it is optional

cards.subject: UK data residency
says: holds primary data in the UK
pins sub-processors to UK or EEA regions where the service supports it
cards.use: answer a buyer who asks where customer data is stored
not: moves customer data to the region with the lowest cost

cards.subject: A data processing agreement
says: is the signed contract setting out how a processor handles personal data
is included with the Enterprise offer
cards.use: supply an enterprise buyer who asks for the paper that governs data handling
not: is the customer's order form for extra MOX

cards.subject: No sale of personal data
says: states that Moksy does not sell personal data
cards.use: answer a customer who asks whether their data is sold
not: allows sale of anonymised profiles to partners

cards.subject: TLS in transit
says: encrypts data moving between a user and the service
is required at version 1.2 or better at Moksy
cards.use: are asked how data is protected on the way to the server
not: encrypts files stored on disk

cards.subject: AES-256 at rest
says: encrypts stored data
covers the primary database and its backups at Moksy
cards.use: are asked how stored data and backups are protected
not: encrypts data moving over the network

cards.subject: Role-based access
says: gives each person only the access their role needs
limits who can see or change sensitive records
cards.use: decide who should be able to read customer data
not: gives every employee the same access

cards.subject: The per-endpoint audit log
says: records requests to each endpoint
supports reconstructing who accessed what
cards.use: need to find out who called a sensitive endpoint last week
not: stores the contents of every customer's Blueprint

cards.subject: The quarterly access review
says: checks every three months who still needs access
catches access left behind after a role change
cards.use: someone changed teams and may still hold old permissions
not: reviews a customer's Blueprint each quarter

cards.subject: Administrator two-factor authentication
says: is mandatory for administrators
adds a second proof of identity beyond a password
cards.use: are setting up an account that can change other people's access
not: is optional for administrators

cards.subject: ISO 27001
says: is an international standard for an information security management system
is a certification Moksy does not yet hold
cards.use: answer a buyer's questionnaire that asks about security certifications
not: is a certification Moksy already holds

cards.subject: Cyber Essentials
says: is a UK basic cyber security certification
is one Moksy has not yet achieved
cards.use: answer a UK public buyer who asks about baseline cyber certification
not: is the standard that governs card payments

cards.subject: Anonymised audit and ledger rows
says: keeps audit and ledger rows after removing the identity
preserves the financial and security record without identifying the person
cards.use: handle a deletion request that touches a row in the audit log
not: deletes the audit row entirely

cards.subject: Card storage
says: leaves card numbers with Stripe
means Moksy does not store them
cards.use: answer a customer who asks whether their card details are kept
not: stores card numbers in Moksy's own database

cards.subject: Defence in depth
says: layers several controls so one failure does not expose everything
assumes any single control can fail
cards.use: are designing protection for a system that holds sensitive data
not: relies on one very strong control at the perimeter

cards.subject: The contracting party
says: is named in the terms and privacy policy as Moksy AI Ltd
is a company registered in England and Wales
cards.use: need to know who the customer's contract is with
not: is the individual reviewer who does the review

cards.subject: Governing law
says: is English law with English courts
cards.use: settle which jurisdiction applies to a dispute over the terms
not: is the law of the country where the customer lives

cards.subject: The minimum age
says: is 18 for customers
cards.use: advise a 16-year-old who wants to open an account
not: is 13 for customers

cards.subject: The customer's content
says: remains owned by the customer
includes the data and content they submit
cards.use: answer a customer who asks who owns what they typed in
not: becomes Moksy's property once submitted

cards.subject: The processing licence
says: is non-exclusive and royalty-free
lets Moksy process submitted content solely to provide the services
cards.use: are asked what Moksy may do with a customer's content
not: lets Moksy sell a customer's content to third parties

cards.subject: The AI-output disclaimer
says: provides AI output for information only without a guarantee
requires the customer to review and validate it before relying on it
cards.use: answer a customer who asks whether they can rely on a Blueprint as professional advice
not: guarantees a Blueprint is accurate for any project

cards.subject: The liability cap
says: limits total liability for a claim to what the customer paid in the previous 12 months
cards.use: respond to a customer who threatens a large claim over a paid plan
not: removes all liability for Moksy in every circumstance

cards.subject: Financial record retention
says: keeps financial records for 7 years
cards.use: handle a customer who asks to delete everything including invoices
not: deletes financial records at the same time as the account

cards.subject: A conflicting published figure
says: is how the sources treat the data deletion period, which differs between the trust page and the privacy policy
should be confirmed before it is quoted as settled
cards.use: answer a customer who asks exactly when their data will be deleted while the pages disagree
not: is resolved by quoting the shorter period

cards.subject: Pricing currency and VAT
says: quotes prices in GBP
excludes VAT unless stated
cards.use: answer a customer who asks whether a displayed price includes tax
not: quotes prices in US dollars

cards.subject: Billing in advance
says: charges premium plans monthly or annually ahead of the period
authorises recurring charges until the customer cancels
cards.use: answer a customer who asks when they are charged
not: bills premium plans in arrears at the end of each period

cards.subject: Cancelling a plan
says: can be done at any time in account settings
cards.use: help a customer who wants to stop paying
not: requires a letter to the legal address

cards.subject: Stripe
says: processes the payments for premium plans
keeps card handling away from Moksy
cards.use: are asked who takes card payments
not: is the company that reviews Blueprints

cards.subject: Invoicing against a purchase order
says: bills Enterprise customers by invoice rather than a card
fits buyers whose procurement requires a PO
cards.use: bill an enterprise buyer who cannot pay by card
not: is how the Free plan is billed

cards.subject: MOX
says: is Moksy credit bought once and not renewed
is pegged at 1 MOX = $0.01
cards.use: need to know what Moksy credit is worth
not: renews every month with the plan

cards.subject: The Wallet ledger
says: itemises every MOX debit
cards.use: answer a customer who asks where their MOX went
not: shows only the current balance

cards.subject: Escrow
says: holds a review fee until the review is accepted or the response window closes without a dispute
cards.use: ask when a reviewer is paid for a job
not: pays the reviewer as soon as they claim the job

cards.subject: A discretionary refund
says: is how unused MOX credit is reviewed through support
is not automatic
cards.use: handle a customer who asks for money back on unused MOX
not: is paid automatically on request

cards.subject: The reviewer hold
says: delays withdrawal of earnings by 14, 7 or 3 days depending on membership
cards.use: answer a reviewer who asks why earnings are not yet available to withdraw
not: pays out earnings the moment a review is accepted

cards.subject: Max plan eligibility
says: makes the Max plan the one that allows someone to become a paid reviewer
cards.use: answer a customer who asks how to start earning as a reviewer
not: is open to every Free plan member

cards.subject: An append-only ledger
says: adds entries without editing past ones
corrects a mistake with a new reversing entry
cards.use: need a money record that can be audited later
not: lets an old entry be overwritten when it is wrong

cards.subject: Reviewer-first hiring
says: starts every job at Moksy with a reviewer account
hires from reviewers who review real plans well
cards.use: are asked how someone gets a job at Moksy
not: starts with a take-home coding test

cards.subject: The fourteen disciplines
says: are the roles Moksy hires into, from Solution architect to Business analyst
are each offered at junior, mid-weight and senior levels
cards.use: are asked which roles Moksy hires for
not: are limited to developers and designers

cards.subject: The unpaid-test ban
says: rules out asking candidates for unpaid work as a test
cards.use: respond to a manager who wants a candidate to build a free prototype
not: is waived for senior candidates

cards.subject: The no-favouritism accreditation rule
says: forbids granting accreditation because Moksy likes someone
cards.use: respond to a friend of a colleague who asks to be accredited without the usual evidence
not: lets a manager accredit anyone they trust

cards.subject: The no-ghost-vacancy rule
says: forbids keeping a vacancy open that Moksy does not intend to fill
cards.use: are asked to keep a job advert live to collect CVs
not: allows adverts to stay open to build a talent pool

cards.subject: A structured interview
says: asks every candidate the same questions scored against the same criteria
reduces the effect of first impressions
cards.use: want fairer comparison between candidates
not: lets each interviewer choose their own questions

cards.subject: A work sample
says: asks a candidate to do a realistic piece of the job under assessment
predicts job performance better than an unstructured chat
cards.use: want evidence of how a candidate actually works
not: is a free project used for the company's own benefit

cards.subject: A job scorecard
says: lists the outcomes and skills a role needs before hiring starts
gives interviewers the same yardstick
cards.use: are about to open a new vacancy
not: is written after the offer is made

cards.subject: A reference check
says: asks former colleagues to confirm a candidate's record
is best done after an offer is in prospect
cards.use: want independent evidence about a candidate's past work
not: replaces the interview

cards.subject: Onboarding
says: helps a new starter become productive and understand the organisation
cards.use: prepare for a new person who starts on Monday
not: begins only when the probation ends

cards.subject: A 30-60-90 plan
says: sets goals for a new starter's first 30, 60 and 90 days
cards.use: want a new hire to know what good looks like early
not: sets goals for the whole first year

cards.subject: Offboarding
says: removes access, collects equipment and hands over knowledge when someone leaves
closes the gap in which a leaver could still reach systems
cards.use: someone has handed in their notice
not: starts when the final payslip is issued

cards.subject: The Docker-first rule
says: runs everything in Docker
forbids running npm install on the host
cards.use: handle a case where a new developer wants to install packages directly on their laptop
not: lets each developer choose between Docker and a host install

cards.subject: The seven mandatory secrets
says: must be filled in .env before the local stack will start
cards.use: handle a case where the local stack refuses to start after copying .env.example
not: are generated automatically during npm run dev

cards.subject: The local quick start
says: copies .env.example to .env, then runs npm run dev, npm run seed and npm run seed:personas
cards.use: set up a working local Moksy stack for the first time
not: begins with a production deploy

cards.subject: The manual deployment rule
says: means pushing to GitHub deploys nothing
needs someone to run the deploy on the server
cards.use: handle a case where a developer assumes merging to main will release the change
not: deploys automatically on every push

cards.subject: npm run deploy:prod
says: rebuilds only the changed services
health-checks them and records the commit
cards.use: need to release a change to the production server
not: rebuilds every service on each run

cards.subject: The plan-only preview
says: shows what a production deploy would do without doing it
cards.use: want to see which services a deploy would touch before running it
not: performs the deploy and reports afterwards

cards.subject: The Moksy Lexicon
says: is the shared vocabulary for the product
settles which word a screen should use
cards.use: handle a case where two screens call the same thing by different names
not: is the list of services in the platform

cards.subject: The brand guidelines
says: set the voice and visual rules for anything Moksy publishes
cards.use: are writing copy or building a page for Moksy
not: describe how services talk to each other

cards.subject: docs/SEO.md
says: records the growth motion and how guide results are tracked
cards.use: need the written plan for how guides are meant to attract customers
not: lists the platform's API endpoints

cards.subject: The developer documentation site
says: is the public Docusaurus site for developers
cards.use: handle a case where a developer needs the published reference for the platform
not: is an internal notebook of private decisions

cards.subject: The published pages
says: are the company's public statements
include pricing, trust, help, legal terms, privacy, reviewer pages and careers
cards.use: need to know what Moksy has said publicly
not: are drafts that staff may rewrite freely

cards.subject: A single source of truth
says: keeps one authoritative copy of a fact that other places point to
stops copies drifting apart
cards.use: handle a case where the same figure appears in four documents and they disagree
not: copies the fact into every document for convenience

cards.subject: A runbook
says: gives step-by-step instructions for a recurring operational task
cards.use: handle a case where an on-call person must restart a service at night
not: records why a past decision was made

cards.subject: A blameless post-incident review
says: examines what happened after an incident without assigning blame to a person
produces actions that change the system
cards.use: handle a case where an outage has just been resolved
not: names the person who made the mistake and ends there

cards.subject: A definition of done
says: lists what must be true before work counts as finished
cards.use: handle a case where a team keeps arguing about whether a task is complete
not: is a list of tasks for the next sprint

cards.subject: A risk register
says: lists known risks with an owner and a response
cards.use: need one place to see what could go wrong and who is handling it
not: records only risks that have already happened

cards.subject: A risk owner
says: is the person accountable for managing one risk
cards.use: handle a case where a risk has been logged and nobody is handling it
not: is the person who first noticed the risk

cards.subject: Likelihood and impact
says: are the two scales used to rank how serious a risk is
cards.use: need to decide which of two risks to deal with first
not: measure how long a risk has been on the register

cards.subject: Risk mitigation
says: reduces the likelihood or impact of a risk
cards.use: decide to add a control to make a risk less damaging
not: accepts the risk without any action

cards.subject: Risk acceptance
says: knowingly tolerates a risk because its cost to remove is higher than its harm
cards.use: decide to live with a small risk and record the decision
not: ignores the risk without recording it

cards.subject: Residual risk
says: is the risk that remains after controls are applied
cards.use: handle a case where a control is in place and you ask how much risk is left
not: is the risk before any control exists

cards.subject: A single point of failure
says: is one component whose failure stops the whole system or service
cards.use: find that one person holds the only copy of a key password
not: is a component with a backup ready to take over

cards.subject: A key-person risk
says: arises when important knowledge or access sits with one individual
cards.use: only one engineer knows how to run the production deploy
not: arises when a team has too many people

cards.subject: The partial-microservice risk
says: records the platform as about 60 percent of the way to a proper microservice architecture
cites a shared secret between services, plain http and no message broker
cards.use: are asked about the biggest architecture risk in the register
not: records that the platform has no database at all

cards.subject: The guest-quota risk
says: records that guest AI quotas reset with each new session
leaves inference spend uncapped and the free tier open to farming
cards.use: someone warns that anonymous visitors can run up AI costs
not: records that paid customers can exceed their quota

cards.subject: The disagreeing-pages risk
says: records that published pages disagree on facts such as the data deletion period
is handled by quoting pages as published and dated
cards.use: support is about to quote a figure that other pages contradict
not: is resolved by removing the pages

cards.subject: The missing-certification risk
says: records that Moksy has neither ISO 27001 nor Cyber Essentials
is answered by saying so plainly on the trust page
cards.use: handle a case where a buyer's security questionnaire asks about certification
not: is answered by implying certification is under way

cards.subject: The pattern dispatcher migration
says: moves the live customer path onto the pattern dispatcher
started from a measured coverage of 0 percent in the 2026-09-14 brief
cards.use: are asked what the architecture brief wants done with the live customer path
not: retires the pattern registry

cards.subject: The six plain rungs
says: replace twenty fantasy rung titles with the lexicon's Candidate to Fellow
differ from the five rungs the published Levels page currently shows
cards.use: are asked how the reviewer ladder titles are meant to change
not: add more themed titles to the ladder

cards.subject: Wave 2 of the cost guides
says: adds SaaS MVP, marketplace, school website and mobile app versus web app
cards.use: are asked which cost guides come after the first wave
not: covers only the booking system and e-commerce guides

cards.subject: The Facebook Page import
says: does not exist today
would need Meta App Review
cards.use: someone wants an ad to promise importing a Facebook Page
not: is a live feature that ads may mention

cards.subject: The enterprise and public sector offer
says: is priced separately
includes SSO, UK data residency and a private reviewer pool
cards.use: handle a case where a public sector buyer asks what is different from the standard plans
not: uses the same price list as Pro

cards.subject: A recorded direction
says: says where work is heading without promising a date
cards.use: read an item on a roadmap that has no delivery date
not: is a committed delivery date

cards.subject: A now-next-later roadmap
says: groups work by time horizon rather than by exact dates
cards.use: want to share a plan without committing to dates
not: gives every item a fixed day of delivery

cards.subject: A dependency
says: is work that must finish before other work can start
cards.use: handle a case where a piece of work cannot begin until another team delivers
not: is a task that can always run in parallel

cards.subject: The Moksy journey
says: runs Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build in that order
cards.use: are asked what happens after a customer types in an Idea
not: starts with Build and ends with Idea

cards.subject: The Briefing
says: is where Moksy asks the questions and gathers the Brief
cards.use: handle a case where a customer answers questions about their idea
not: is the AI-drafted plan itself

cards.subject: The Blueprint
says: is the build-ready plan drafted by AI from the Brief
covers up to 22 Areas
cards.use: handle a case where a customer asks what Moksy produces from their answers
not: is the questionnaire the customer fills in

cards.subject: A Project
says: holds one idea and its Blueprint
cards.use: handle a case where a customer starts working on a second idea
not: holds every idea a customer will ever have

cards.subject: Peer Review
says: is free and comes from the community
cards.use: handle a case where a customer wants a review at no charge
not: is done only by accredited reviewers

cards.subject: Expert Review
says: is done by an accredited reviewer
is included in Pro and Max
cards.use: handle a case where a customer wants an accredited reviewer to check their Blueprint
not: is a free review from the community

cards.subject: Priority Review
says: is paid and returns an Expert Review within 36 hours
cards.use: handle a case where a customer needs an accredited review back the next day
not: is included free in every plan

cards.subject: A Spec Sprint
says: is a one-day, human-led engagement
cards.use: handle a case where a customer wants a person rather than the AI to work on their specification
not: is a month-long managed build

cards.subject: Build
says: covers exports, hiring and tools
cards.use: handle a case where a customer has an accepted Blueprint and wants to act on it
not: is the step where the AI asks questions

cards.subject: An AI-drafted Blueprint
says: is a draft that can be wrong
shows its reasoning on every recommendation
cards.use: handle a case where a customer asks whether a Blueprint is guaranteed correct
not: is a finished, verified specification

cards.subject: A Guest
says: is someone who is not signed in
cards.use: describe a visitor using the site without an account
not: is anyone with a Project

cards.subject: A Member
says: is someone signed in on the Free plan
cards.use: describe a signed-in person who has not paid
not: is an accredited reviewer

cards.subject: A Customer
says: is anyone with a Project
cards.use: describe a person who has started an idea in Moksy
not: is someone not signed in

cards.subject: A Reviewer
says: is an accredited person who reviews Blueprints
cards.use: describe someone who claims jobs from the Queue
not: is an operator of Moksy

cards.subject: Staff
says: is the word for an operator of Moksy
cards.use: describe someone who runs the platform rather than using it
not: is anyone who has a Project

cards.subject: A super admin
says: is staff who can pin a user to a level
cards.use: need someone who can override automatic level computation
not: is a customer on the Max plan

qa.q: A visitor asks what problem Moksy exists to solve. Which answer matches the mission?
qa.right: Most software fails in the specification, so Moksy turns an idea into a build-ready plan
wrong: Most software is too slow, so Moksy hosts it on faster servers
Most agencies charge too much, so Moksy builds software cheaply
Most startups lack funding, so Moksy lends them money to build
qa.why: The mission locates the failure in the specification, not the implementation.

qa.q: A customer on the Free plan cannot sign in. Where should they write?
qa.right: The support address
wrong: The privacy address
The legal address
Sales
qa.why: Account and sign-in problems go to support.

qa.q: A customer asks for a copy of all the personal data Moksy holds about them. Where should the request go?
qa.right: The privacy address
wrong: The support address
The legal address
Sales
qa.why: Privacy and data requests have their own address.

qa.q: A customer asks what a clause in the terms means. Which address handles that?
qa.right: The legal address
wrong: The privacy address
The support address
The help centre
qa.why: Questions about the terms go to the legal address.

qa.q: A 17-year-old wants to open a Moksy account for a school project. What does the minimum age rule say?
qa.right: Customers must be at least 18
wrong: Customers must be at least 13
Customers must be at least 16 with a parent's consent
There is no minimum age for the Free plan
qa.why: The terms set 18 as the minimum age.

qa.q: Put the Moksy journey in order.
qa.right: Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build
wrong: Briefing, Idea, Review, Blueprint, Build
Idea, Blueprint, Briefing, Build, Review
Build, Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review
qa.why: The five steps always run in that order.

qa.q: A new developer wants to run npm install directly on their laptop to start the Moksy stack. What is the rule?
qa.right: Everything runs in Docker, so do not run npm install on the host
wrong: Run npm install on the host, then start Docker
Use the host install for the frontend and Docker for the services
Either approach is fine if the secrets are filled in
qa.why: The Docker-first rule forbids a host npm install.

qa.q: A customer asks whether Moksy sells the data they enter. What is the accurate answer?
qa.right: No, Moksy does not sell personal data
wrong: Only anonymised data is sold to partners
Data is sold only if the customer is on the Free plan
Data is sold to the reviewers who check the Blueprint
qa.why: The profile states that personal data is not sold.

qa.q: A marketer wants to add the line "Moksy will import your Facebook Page" to an ad. What should you say?
qa.right: No, the Facebook Page import does not exist and an ad may only describe what exists
wrong: Yes, as long as the ad says coming soon
Yes, because it is on the roadmap
Yes, if the figures in the ad come from a source
qa.why: Ads may only describe what exists and can be evidenced.

qa.q: A new guide has been live for two weeks and shows no Blueprints started. What does the review cadence say?
qa.right: Nothing is expected for four to eight weeks, so wait for the 4, 8 and 12-week reviews
wrong: The guide has failed and should be rewritten now
Spend on paid social to speed up the results
Remove the guide until the crawler visits it
qa.why: Earlier numbers measure the crawler's schedule, not the content.

qa.q: Which is the best description of the 1:99 goal?
qa.right: 99 percent of the work done by machine and 1 percent by a human
wrong: 1 percent of visitors become customers and 99 percent do not
One reviewer checking 99 Blueprints a day
A price of £1 for the first 99 customers
qa.why: It is the founder's automation target.

qa.q: A customer asks who owns the idea they typed into Moksy. What is the right answer?
qa.right: The customer; Moksy claims no rights over the plan or the idea behind it
wrong: Moksy, because it produced the Blueprint
Both owners equally, split 50/50
The reviewer who checked the Blueprint
qa.why: The no-rights rule holds on every plan.

qa.q: A buyer's procurement team cannot pay by card. How does Moksy bill Enterprise?
qa.right: By invoice against a purchase order
wrong: Only by card with a higher limit
By bank transfer in advance with no invoice
Enterprise customers cannot be billed
qa.why: Enterprise is invoiced against a PO.

qa.q: Which is true of MOX?
qa.right: It is bought once, does not renew and is pegged at 1 MOX = $0.01
wrong: It renews monthly with the plan and is pegged to the pound
It is earned only by reviewers and cannot be bought
It expires after 30 days and is refunded automatically
qa.why: MOX is a one-off credit with a fixed peg.

qa.q: Which of these is a signed-in person on the Free plan who has not started a Project?
qa.right: A Member
wrong: A Guest
A Customer
A Reviewer
qa.why: A Guest is not signed in; a Customer has a Project.

qa.q: Support is about to tell a customer that their data will be deleted in 30 days, but the privacy policy says 90. What should support do?
qa.right: Quote the published pages as dated, say they differ and confirm before promising
wrong: Quote the shorter period to reassure the customer
Quote the longer period to be safe
Pick the figure that sounds most likely and say nothing about the other
qa.why: Support must not state a figure as settled when the published pages disagree.

qa.q: A reviewer and a customer disagree about whether a review was fair. Who settles it?
qa.right: A senior reviewer, whose ruling decides whether the review counts as accepted
wrong: The original reviewer, who knows the Blueprint best
The customer, because they paid for it
The next customer who uses the same template
qa.why: Disputed reviews go to support and are arbitrated by a senior reviewer.

qa.q: A reviewer asks why the fee for an accepted review is not yet in their balance. What holds it?
qa.right: Escrow holds the fee until the review is accepted or the response window closes without a dispute
wrong: The Wallet ledger holds it until month end
The support address must approve each payment by hand
The fee is paid only when the customer upgrades to Max
qa.why: Escrow releases fees on acceptance or an undisputed window closing.

qa.q: A candidate offers to build a free prototype to prove their skills. What is Moksy's position?
qa.right: Moksy does not ask for unpaid work as a test
wrong: Moksy accepts it if the candidate offers
Moksy asks for it only from senior candidates
Moksy asks for it only from reviewers
qa.why: The unpaid-test ban is a stated hiring commitment.

qa.q: A buyer's security questionnaire asks whether Moksy is ISO 27001 certified. What is the accurate reply?
qa.right: Not yet; the trust page says so plainly
wrong: Yes, the certificate is held by a sub-processor
Certification is in the final stage, so yes
ISO 27001 is not relevant to Moksy
qa.why: Moksy is not ISO 27001 certified and not yet Cyber Essentials certified.

qa.q: A developer merges a fix to the main branch and assumes it is live. Why is that wrong at Moksy?
qa.right: Pushing to GitHub deploys nothing; someone must run the deploy on the server
wrong: The fix must first be approved by Stripe
Deploys run only on Fridays
The fix goes live only after a Peer Review
qa.why: Deployment is manual.

qa.q: A team member proposes cold-calling startups to reach the subscriber target. What does the growth thinking say?
qa.right: Outbound cannot reach the number of subscribers the published prices need, so growth is a content and search problem
wrong: Cold-calling is the main plan and content is secondary
Outbound is fine if the calls are recorded
Cold-calling is only banned for the Enterprise offer
qa.why: Outbound sales is a documented non-goal.

qa.q: Which pair of facts describes the Briefing and the Blueprint correctly?
qa.right: The Briefing gathers the Brief through questions; the Blueprint is the AI-drafted plan built from it
wrong: The Briefing is the finished plan; the Blueprint is the questionnaire
Both are the same document with two names
The Briefing is a human-led one-day engagement; the Blueprint is a review
qa.why: The Briefing asks; the Blueprint is drafted from the answers.

qa.q: An engineer wants to see which services a production deploy would touch without deploying. What should they use?
qa.right: The plan-only preview of the production deploy
wrong: Run the production deploy and cancel it halfway
Run npm install on the server
Ask support to check the services
qa.why: A plan-only preview exists for deploy:prod.

qa.q: Two documents give different figures for the same support target. Which practice fixes the cause?
qa.right: Keep a single source of truth and have the other documents point to it
wrong: Copy the figure into every document by hand
Delete the older document and keep working
Let each team keep its own figure
qa.why: One authoritative copy stops drift.

qa.q: Which is the best example of a leading indicator for Moksy's growth?
qa.right: Impressions on a new guide
wrong: Pro subscribers at year end
Annual revenue
Customers lost this quarter
qa.why: Impressions move before the Blueprints and upgrades they predict.

qa.q: A manager asks one person to both raise and approve a payment to save time. What control does that break?
qa.right: Separation of duties
wrong: Data minimisation
Defence in depth
A recorded direction
qa.why: One person should not complete every step of a sensitive process.

qa.q: A customer deletes their account and asks for every record to be erased, including invoices. What happens to the financial records?
qa.right: They are kept for the retention period because financial records must be held for 7 years
wrong: They are deleted at once with the account
They are posted to the customer
They are anonymised and deleted after 30 days
qa.why: The profile records a 7-year retention for financial records.

qa.q: A customer exercises their right to deletion, but the audit log holds rows about them. What does Moksy do with those rows?
qa.right: Anonymises them rather than deleting them
wrong: Deletes them so no trace remains
Leaves them unchanged with the name visible
Moves them to the support mailbox
qa.why: Audit and ledger rows are anonymised, not deleted.

qa.q: A personal-data breach is discovered on a Friday evening. What is the rule that sets the clock?
qa.right: Article 33: notification within 72 hours of becoming aware
wrong: Notification within 30 days of the breach being resolved
Notification at the next quarterly access review
Notification only if the ICO asks
qa.why: The 72-hour window starts when the organisation becomes aware.

qa.q: Someone wants to add a new supplier that will process customer data. What does Moksy require?
qa.right: Thirty days' notice before adding a sub-processor
wrong: No notice, since suppliers are internal
Immediate notice after the supplier goes live
Approval from the ICO first
qa.why: Adding a sub-processor takes 30 days' notice.

qa.q: A reviewer on a short hold period asks why their earnings arrive sooner than a colleague's. What decides the delay?
qa.right: The reviewer's membership sets a hold of 14, 7 or 3 days
wrong: The size of the review decides the delay
The customer decides the delay when accepting
The delay is always 14 days
qa.why: Hold length depends on membership.

qa.q: A product lead wants a recorded roadmap item to show as promised for next month. What is wrong with that?
qa.right: The item is a recorded direction, not a committed date
wrong: Roadmap items can never be shared
Only the founder may read the roadmap
Directions are always ranked by cost
qa.why: The sources record directions, not committed dates.

qa.q: A support agent tells a customer that Priority Review is free with their Pro plan. What is wrong?
qa.right: Priority Review is paid; Expert Review is the one included in Pro
wrong: Priority Review is free only on Max
Priority Review is included for new customers
Nothing is wrong
qa.why: Priority Review is paid and returns an Expert Review within 36 hours.

qa.q: An ad draft says "Reviews cost only X MOX". Which rule does it break?
qa.right: Do not quote review values in ads; the promise is the free Blueprint
wrong: All ads must quote prices
Ads may not mention MOX at all
Ads may only mention Priority Review
qa.why: The ad rules say not to quote review values.

qa.q: The risk register lists a risk with no owner. What is the right next step?
qa.right: Assign a named owner who is accountable for managing it
wrong: Delete the risk until someone volunteers
Mark the risk as accepted
Leave it for the quarterly access review
qa.why: A risk with no owner is a risk nobody is managing.

qa.q: Engineers argue about whether to keep the shared secret between services because replacing it is costly. Which concept describes the choice to live with it?
qa.right: Risk acceptance, ideally recorded with an owner
wrong: Risk mitigation
Residual risk
Delegation of authority
qa.why: Knowingly tolerating a risk is acceptance.

qa.q: Guest AI quotas reset with every new session. Which consequence does the register record?
qa.right: Inference spend is uncapped and the free tier can be farmed
wrong: Paid customers lose their quota
Reviewers are paid twice
Blueprints become public
qa.why: Resetting quotas let anonymous visitors consume AI spend.

qa.q: A buyer asks where customer data is held. Which answer is most complete and accurate?
qa.right: Primary data is held in the UK, and sub-processors are pinned to UK or EEA regions wherever the service supports it
wrong: All data is held in the UK with no exceptions
Data is held wherever is cheapest
Data is held in the US with a UK backup
qa.why: The qualification about sub-processors matters; avoid overstating.

qa.q: A customer finds the trust page and privacy policy disagree on the deletion period and demands one answer today. What is the most defensible response?
qa.right: Explain that the published pages differ, state each as published and dated, and confirm the correct figure before committing
wrong: Pick the shorter period so the customer is satisfied
Say the pages are identical
Refuse to discuss deletion until the pages are fixed
qa.why: Quote what is published and confirm before promising.

qa.q: The partial-microservice risk lists a shared secret, plain http and no message broker. Which fix addresses the plain http?
qa.right: Encrypted transport between services
wrong: A second shared secret
A larger gateway controller
Moving to a single database
qa.why: Plain http between services is fixed by encrypting the transport.

qa.q: A recruiter wants to leave a role advertised for months to build a pool of CVs, with no plan to hire soon. Which Moksy commitment does this go against?
qa.right: Moksy will not keep a vacancy open that it does not intend to fill
wrong: Moksy will not advertise roles at all
Moksy will not interview candidates twice
Moksy will not hire from reviewer accounts
qa.why: Keeping a ghost vacancy open is ruled out.

qa.q: A reviewer has the Max plan and asks whether that alone makes them a paid reviewer. What is the accurate position?
qa.right: Max makes someone eligible to become a paid reviewer; eligibility is not the same as being accredited
wrong: Max automatically makes them an accredited reviewer
Max is irrelevant to paid reviewing
Only Pro members can become paid reviewers
qa.why: Max gives eligibility, not accreditation.

qa.q: Why does Moksy keep a decidedBy stamp on every decision rather than estimating the machine share?
qa.right: So the 1:99 share is measured rather than guessed
wrong: So customers can see which reviewer approved them
So support can refund MOX faster
So the ICO can audit every Blueprint
qa.why: The stamp is the measurement behind the goal.

qa.q: A launch proposal offers a big free-tier promotion. Which recorded risk should be raised first?
qa.right: Guest AI quotas reset on a new session, so spend is uncapped and the free tier can be farmed
wrong: The Facebook Page import does not exist
The missing Cyber Essentials certificate
The rung titles are fantasy names
qa.why: A public free tier combined with uncapped guest quotas is the direct exposure.
